edu.desc: Dissertation: delivery slot planning to reduce empty runs

exp.desc:
- Payment provider integration
- Tests and error handling
- Code reviews

cl.p1: My dissertation answered a question your product asks every day: how do you plan delivery slots so fewer vans drive empty? I built a planning service in Python and tested it on anonymised data from a delivery company; empty runs dropped noticeably in simulation.
cl.p2: As a student and part-time developer I built REST APIs with PostgreSQL and Docker, with good test coverage because I like to sleep at night. At my part-time job I integrated a payment provider and learned how much error handling matters when money is involved.
cl.p3: My code is public – the link is on my CV. I would be glad to talk about the role.

cl.p1: For ten years I mixed live concerts as a sound engineer. When venues closed, I started coding – first out of curiosity, then with a plan: a year of self-study and a twelve-week full-time bootcamp.
cl.p2: My final project is a rehearsal-room booking tool that a music charity has used for six months. I built it with JavaScript, Node and a small database and still maintain it; users report bugs straight to me, which is the most honest code review there is.
cl.p3: I know I am starting as a junior. An agency with many small projects would be the best place for me to learn fast.
